reasons: Worth one measurement. It is the first test of the tfx_daily dimension: a named forced-liquidation mechanism (a levered retail book that grew into a decline is latent losscut supply), a sign fixed before any run, and a same-decline control. It is not a duplicate. jpy_cross_losscut_after_us_shock conditioned on a US equity shock and held one Tokyo session; this conditions on the retail book itself and holds days. It does share that test's population, side and Tokyo-open short, and that test found the crosses bounce in the Tokyo morning after US-session selloffs (all 12 arms lost). That is a known headwind in the first hours of this trade.

Premise check on tfx_daily (descriptive, conditioning data only). The dip-buying signature, a negative yearly correlation between the daily return and the open-interest change, holds in every year 2010-2023 for AUDJPY (-0.40 to -0.78) and NZDJPY (-0.23 to -0.70). USDJPY's flips from 2017 (+0.36 in 2017, about 0 in 2018, +0.35 to +0.72 in 2019-2023, matching the weekly long_share of 0.19-0.37 since 2022). GBPJPY is about 0 in 2016-2017, and EURJPY is positive from 2013. As a result the USDJPY heavy bands never fire in 2018-2023 (0 qualifying days). Check evidence comes from AUDJPY (about 37 heavy10 trades at k 1.0, hold 2), NZDJPY (about 53) and GBPJPY (about 18). Even AUDJPY was only about half long on the first weekly reading (long_share 0.51 on 2022-11-22), so 'structurally long' is an assumption about the design years.

Rule bug: the leftover guard exit_short[sig_k] closes the open trade at the next qualifying row's fill bar. The executor registers that row's entry only if it is flat at the signal bar's close, so the new row is not traded either. Five-day declines qualify on runs of consecutive days, so most 2- and 4-day holds would be cut to about one day and every other qualifying day skipped. The hold the hypothesis is about would not be the one tested.

Counts are below the brief. Friday rows (20% of TFX rows) are skipped, and one-position holds de-overlap. On AUDJPY in design with the planned-hold de-overlap: heavy10 91/70 trades (hold 2/4), heavy15 61/45 and light 29/26 at k 1.0; 67/53, 49/37 and 21/18 at k 1.5. Trading Friday rows at the Monday 00:00 UTC open gives 100/76, 66/48 and 35/28 (k 1.0) and 73/57, 51/38 and 24/19 (k 1.5). At +0.08 R the expected design t is about 0.7-0.9, below the stage A floor of 1.0 more often than not even if the effect is real.

Control too small and confounded. With 19-35 light trades the heavy-minus-light difference has a standard error of about 0.2 R, against a +0.06 R gate. And retail buys bigger dips, so heavy days are deeper declines: on AUDJPY at k 1.0 the median drop is -1.89 ATR (heavy10) and -2.08 (heavy15) against -1.65 (light) in design, and -2.37 against -1.43 in check. A raw heavy-minus-light difference partly measures decline size. Pooled over the four crosses the light arm has about 240 design trades (standard error about 0.075 R).

EURJPY as a placebo inside spec.markets would enter the pipeline's automatic gates. Stage B picks its best heavy cell. If that cell is positive in design, its trades join the pooled check and walk-forward, and it must also pass the 1.5x-cost gate. A placebo must be able neither to pass the hypothesis nor to kill it.

The mechanism pays in the tail: the BIS losscut evidence is about cascades (2011-08, 2013-05/06, 2015-08, 2016-01/02, 2016-06). Kill rule (3) drops the best tenth of dates, so a real but tail-only effect fails by construction. That fits the speed goal, but the lesson has to be recorded as tail-only, not as no effect.

Speed is far below the bar: about 1 trade a month per cross, 0.16 at expectation, +0.35 R needed to reach 0.7. This is an edge-recording test, and its main value is fixing the baseline for the TFX dimension.

Costs are low: the AUDJPY opening spread at 00:00 UTC had a median of 1.2-1.4 pips (p90 1.8-1.9) in 2012-2017. The round trip is about 2.5 pips against a stop of about 81 pips, about 0.03 R. Swap on the short is small over 2-4 days.
revisions: BUILDER (implement exactly): (R1) Replace the leftover guard with a planned-hold de-overlap. Walk the qualifying rows of the active band in time order. Keep a row only if it passes every skip rule and m.ts[sig] >= target_prev, the exit target of the last KEPT row; for the first kept row there is no condition. A dropped row sets no entry and no markers, and a trade stopped early does not reopen the window. For kept rows only, set exit_short[xi_k - 1] = True, plus the causal fallback on every bar j with m.ts[j] >= target_k and j <= the sig of the next kept row (m.n - 1 for the last). No separate leftover guard. (R2) Trade Friday rows at the Monday Tokyo open. T* = the first 00:00 UTC at or after ts_avail that falls on Monday to Friday: T* = ts_avail for Monday-Thursday rows and the following Monday 00:00 UTC for Friday rows. sig = the bar whose close time == T* (the 23:00-00:00 UTC bar; on Sunday night it belongs to Monday's trading day). Otherwise use the first bar whose close time is >= T*, within max_delay_min of T* and on T*'s UTC date, else skip. D = daily.day_idx[sig] - 1, and still require daily.date[D] == the row's date. This adds about 20-25% of qualifying days and changes nothing else. (R3) PARAMS and GRID unchanged. DIRECTOR: (R4) Edit specs/auto/jpy_retail_dipbuy_fragility.json after this review. stage_a = {market: AUDJPY, grid: all 12 cells}; grid = {band: [heavy10, heavy15], k: [1.0, 1.5], hold_days: [2, 4]}; markets = [AUDJPY, NZDJPY, USDJPY, GBPJPY]. Take EURJPY out of spec.markets, because the pipeline would pool a design-positive placebo into G2, G2b and G4. Run EURJPY report-only: the chosen heavy cell and its light cell with end = 2024-01-01, counted as trials, not gated. (R5) Restate the expectations, AUDJPY design after R1-R2: heavy10 about 100/76 trades (hold 2/4) at k 1.0 and 73/57 at k 1.5; heavy15 66/48 and 51/38 (the k 1.5, hold 4 heavy15 cell is below 40 trades and cannot be chosen); light 35/28 and 24/19. Expected design t at +0.08 R about 0.7-0.9. Check heavy10 trades at k 1.0, hold 2: AUDJPY about 37, NZDJPY about 53, GBPJPY about 18, USDJPY 0, because the USDJPY book turned net short from 2017. In rule (4), USDJPY counts as a design-only replication market. (R6) Mechanism gate (rule 2) before any promotion: if the heavy arm passes B/C, run the matching light cell (same k and hold_days) on NZDJPY, USDJPY and GBPJPY with end = 2024-01-01, counted as trials. Require the pooled four-cross heavy-minus-light difference to be >= +0.06 R in design and > 0 in check, computed within decline strata: -1.5 < drop_atr <= -1.0, -2.0 < drop_atr <= -1.5 and drop_atr <= -2.0, using the strata the cell's k admits and weighting by the heavy arm's trade shares. Report each arm's median drop_atr. The AUDJPY-only stage A difference is not enough. (R7) Breadth rule (3): list the removed dates. If they are the cascade months (2011-08, 2013-05/06, 2015-08, 2016-01/02, 2016-06) and the remainder is <= 0, record the lesson as 'retail-book fragility is tail-only at a 2-4 day horizon'. Do not retry it with other open-interest thresholds or lookbacks, and never register the long (liquidity-provision) mirror from this run. (R8) Speed is judged by the monthly Sharpe of the pooled R per month after costs; below 0.7 the result is recorded, not traded.
notes_for_builder: 1. Rows: tx = F.ext_series(m, 'tfx_daily'); mask = tx.column('symbol') == m.sym (the column can hold None; compare None-safe); rows = F.ext_subset(m, 'tfx_daily', mask). Raise ValueError if no row matches (the series starts in 2005, so the leak-test truncation never empties it for these crosses). Rows are in ts_avail order. The date column is a datetime; compare it as datetime64[D]. 2. oi_g_r = oi[r] / oi[r - L] - 1 over the previous L = p['oi_lookback'] TFX ROWS (not calendar days). NaN when r < L or when any oi in r-L..r is <= 0. No statistic over the whole sample. 3. daily = F.daily_bars(m); ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, p['atr_n'])). T* as in R2. sig = np.searchsorted(m.close_times(), T*, 'left'); require close_times[sig] - T* <= max_delay_min, close_times[sig] on T*'s UTC date, and sig < m.n - 1. D = daily.day_idx[sig] - 1; require D - ret_lookback >= 0 and daily.date[D] == the row's date. drop_atr = (daily.c[D] - daily.c[D - ret_lookback]) / ATR20[sig]; condition drop_atr <= -k. ATR20[sig] must be finite and > 0. 4. Bands: heavy10 oi_g >= 0.10, heavy15 oi_g >= 0.15, light oi_g <= 0.02; raise ValueError on any other band value. 5. Short only: entry_short[sig] = True, entry_type 0, valid_bars 1, sl_dist = sl_atr x ATR20[sig], tp_dist NaN, max_bars 0. 6. Exit: E = the hold_days-th Monday-to-Friday date after the UTC date of m.ts[sig + 1]; target = E + exit_utc (F.parse_hhmm); xi = np.searchsorted(m.ts, target, 'left'). Keep the row only if xi < m.n and xi > sig + 1. 7. De-overlap per R1 in a Python loop over rows (about 250 a year), then entries and markers for kept rows only. 8. ts_avail = the date + 1 day at 00:00 UTC, which equals the close of the 23:00 UTC bar, so the row is usable on that bar (ts_avail <= close, as in F.ext_asof). Never use a row whose ts_avail is after close_times[sig]. 9. Checker expectations, AUDJPY design 2010-2017 with the defaults (heavy10, k 1.0, hold 2): about 100 trades; heavy15 about 66 and light about 35 at the same k and hold. Read every tunable from p (band, k, hold_days, sl_atr, oi_lookback, ret_lookback, exit_utc, max_delay_min, atr_n).
